Reaction times to high- and low-frequency words

Source: R/data.R
rt_frequency.Rd

A small lexical decision task: 10 participants each respond to the same 20 words, 10 of high and 10 of low frequency.

Usage

rt_frequency

Format

A tibble with 200 rows and 5 columns:

participant

Participant ID, P01 to P10.

word

Word ID, w01 to w20.

frequency

Word frequency, "high" or "low".

rt

Reaction time in ms.

correct

1 for a correct response, 0 for an error.

Source

data-raw/rt_frequency.R

Details

True model: log(rt) = 6.38 + 0.1 * low + p0 + w0 + e, with by-participant intercepts p0 (SD 0.12), by-word intercepts w0 (SD 0.06) and residual SD 0.15, so low-frequency words take about 10% longer. Accuracy is 95% for high- and 85% for low-frequency words.

Examples

aggregate(cbind(rt, correct) ~ frequency, data = rt_frequency, FUN = mean)
#>   frequency     rt correct
#> 1      high 630.86    0.96
#> 2       low 692.68    0.86
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- lme4::lmer(log(rt) ~ frequency + (1 | participant) + (1 | word), data = rt_frequency)
  exp(lme4::fixef(m))
}
#>  (Intercept) frequencylow 
#>   619.355116     1.102924
